text.p: Israeli bonds closed lower on Tuesday with prices of medium and long-term bonds falling slightly while the market awaited the publication of the consumer price index (CPI), traders said. Indices:
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.08 pct to 105.33
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.03 to 104.12
"Today was a day of waiting to see what the CPI will be," said Miri Dagan, a trader at Clal Insurance. The March CPI of 1.0 percent was published after the trading day was over.
"Trading was mixed with a negative trend in medium and long-term bonds, mainly because of the big amount of bond issues this week and last week," she said.

The Bank of Israel issued on behalf of the government on Monday 400 million shekels worth of bonds instead of the usual 200 million shekels because markets will be closed next Monday for the Jewish holiday of Passover.

"The central bank issued the bonds at a price lower than the market price and this caused pressure on the bonds. Prices of long-term bonds fell slightly," said Danny Alt, a portfolio manager at Nesuah Trading and Investment.
He said prices of unlinked bonds were up again due to expectations of an economic package deal that would include a cut in the government budget and in interest rates.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Finance Minister Dan Meridor and Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel met on Sunday and Monday to discuss the budget deficit but no decision was reached. The talks were due to resume on Tuesday.
It was unclear whether any decision to cut the budget would be made at the meeting and the central bank has refused to link a budget cut to a reduction in interest rates.
Demand for dollar-linked bonds continued to rise on the strengthening of the dollar worldwide, traders said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
